## Reading the coordinated pattern

Several signals tend to move **together** around day 7–14: fever and leukocytosis often peak,
and vasospasm/DCI risk (rising TCD velocities, a rising Lindegaard ratio) is at its highest. In
that same window, watch for things trending the **other** way — serum sodium, GCS, and net
fluid balance often drift down as cerebral salt wasting and DCI take hold. Enter today's values
and 48-hour trends in the bar above to see how this patient compares.

A patient whose numbers are **not** moving this way deserves a second look at the differential —
fever without leukocytosis, or a falling GCS without any of the rest, points away from the
textbook pattern and toward something else (seizure, a new bleed, a med effect).
